featured_reviews.review_text:
走進孟買的心臟，你會來到一個讓世界又震撼又敬佩的地方——Dharavi。這裡面積僅約1.75平方公里，卻容納了數十萬人口，是亞洲最密集的社區之一。但如果你只用「貧民窟」來定義它，那就太小看這裡了。

在狹窄巷弄之間，藏著驚人的經濟能量。回收、皮革、紡織、陶器，一間間小工坊日夜運轉，創造出數億美元的產值，產品甚至銷往世界各地。這裡沒有華麗辦公室，卻有最真實的創業精神；沒有資源優勢，卻用雙手打造無限可能。

來自印度各地的人們在此落腳，不同語言、宗教與文化交織，形成獨特的生命力。儘管面對擁擠與衛生挑戰，他們依然努力生活、努力工作，用韌性撐起整個城市的運轉。

達拉維不是悲情的象徵，而是一面鏡子，讓人看見人在困境中依然可以發光。走一趟，你會重新理解什麼叫做努力，什麼叫做希望。
featured_reviews.review_translated_text:
Step into the heart of Mumbai, and you'll find a place that both shocks and inspires awe—Dharavi. Spanning only about 1.75 square kilometers, it houses hundreds of thousands of people, making it one of the most densely populated communities in Asia. But to define it merely as a "slum" would be a gross underestimation.

Hidden within its narrow alleyways is an astonishing economic energy. Recycling, leather, textiles, pottery—small workshops operate day and night, generating hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue, with products sold worldwide. Here, there are no glamorous offices, but the most genuine entrepreneurial spirit; no resource advantages, but limitless possibilities created with their own hands.

People from all over India have settled here, their diverse languages, religions, and cultures intertwining to create a unique vitality. Despite facing overcrowding and sanitation challenges, they persevere, working hard and resiliently keeping the city running.

Dharavi is not a symbol of tragedy, but a mirror reflecting the light that shines even in adversity. A visit will give you a new understanding of the meaning of hard work and hope.

featured_reviews.review_text:
First of all: Highly Recommended!!!

Dharavi is about hard working people, family businesses, migrants from all over India hoping for a better life, making more money in Mumbai. It is about recycling, reusing and producing, about a great community that helps each other! About dancing kids in the monsoon rains and big smiles seeing foreigners talking and playing with them.

It is by far the most moving tour I did, it’s not about seeing poverty, it is about the challenge of life.

I recommended to all my colleagues!

featured_reviews.name: Brett Hansen
featured_reviews.review_text:
We joined the ethical walking tour of Dharavi slums with Reality Tours & Travel and it was one of the most eye opening and meaningful experiences of our time in Mumbai, India.

Our guide Diksha was excellent. She is a young Gen Z woman who is incredibly wise, well informed and very articulate. She explained the social, economic and cultural realities of Dharavi with clarity and compassion, and was always happy to answer questions along the way.

What I appreciated most about this tour is that it focuses primarily on the businesses and industries operating within Dharavi rather than treating it like a spectacle. We saw small scale recycling operations, leather workshops, pottery areas and many other hardworking micro industries. It was fascinating to learn how much manufacturing and production takes place here. At times we also walked through incredibly narrow pathways between homes, sometimes only about a metre wide, which gave a sense of just how densely populated the area is.

Dharavi has an estimated population of between 700,000 and 1 million people living in only about 2.1 square kilometres, so the energy and activity is intense. People work extremely hard. Many workers come from other regions of India, sending money home to their families and only seeing them once or twice a year. Some sleep at their workplaces and work 12 to 15 hour days. It is a tough life and seeing this reality firsthand is humbling.

One of the most confronting things we learned is that materials produced in Dharavi are sometimes used by high end international brands. However, the origin is often labelled simply as “Made in India” rather than Dharavi because of the stigma attached to the area. That was heartbreaking to hear given the skill and effort of the people working there.

Photography and video are not allowed on the tour, which is completely fair and respectful. It keeps the focus on learning rather than treating people’s lives as a spectacle.

Another reason to support this tour is that 80 percent of the profits go back into local education programs run by the organisation. While schooling in India is compulsory, class sizes can be around one teacher to 50 students. Reality Tours supports supplementary learning including English and IT classes, along with scholarships for local students.

The tour was scheduled for about 90 minutes but ended up running for closer to two hours and fifteen minutes, so we were definitely tired by the end, but it was absolutely worth it.

If you want to better understand a part of Mumbai that many visitors never see, this slum tour is thoughtful, respectful and genuinely educational. It reminds you that there are whole worlds of experience beyond our own daily lives, and that they are worth learning about with empathy and respect.

It was fascinating to see how much industry, creativity and entrepreneurship thrive within Dharavi — from small workshops and recycling businesses to local artisans creating amazing products. We gained a completely new perspective on the strength, dignity and optimism of the community.

Janna was an absolutely fantastic guide — professional, knowledgeable, patient and genuinely kind. His explanations were detailed and engaging and he answered all our questions with warmth and enthusiasm. We were provided with water during the tour and our driver was always ready to take us to the next stop.

Overall, this tour gave us a much deeper understanding of Mumbai and its people. It was a privilege to see this side of the city through such honest and respectful storytelling. We absolutely and wholeheartedly recommend Citypulse Tours.

featured_reviews.name: Mike Cahill
featured_reviews.review_text: I am fortunate to get to visit Mumbai for work once or twice a year and I always make a point of taking a tour. Mubeen is extremely friendly, helpful and knowledgable and the tours are always excellent. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Kiki
featured_reviews.review_text: I did their Night market tour with Bala and it was amazing! He was very knowledgeable and we learned a lot about food, culinary culture as well as the city itself we would’ve otherwise known. The food we tried was also very delicious. It is a must tour. Thank you Bala!

featured_reviews.name: Danny Riding
featured_reviews.review_text: We had two excellent days of touring with Mubeen! He’s a great tour guide (the best we’ve had on many Asian travels) with an in-depth knowledge of Bombay. We packed so much into our long weekend and saw sides to the city that tourists would be unlikely to find on their own. He listened carefully to what we wanted and designed a bespoke itinerary (and was happy to change it last-minute to accommodate our preferences). There’s so much to see in Bombay - I’d recommend you include Mubeen in your travel plans to get the most out of your time in this brilliant city.

featured_reviews.name: winson koon
featured_reviews.review_text: Mubeen my Mumbai local guide is expert in Mumbai travel. With his knowleadge ,he managed to well arrange and organise the trip based on individual preference. I'm glad that with my tie schedule still managed to cover the places (dharavi slums,dorby ghut and south bombay) as my wish list. Mubeen willing to share the history and whatever he know about the city. Travel with Mubeen is "eye-opening" journey. High recommend to whom wish to travel Mumbai and experience the city in local way. Thanks Mubeen ,keep up the good work!

featured_reviews.name: Jesse Miller
featured_reviews.review_text:
My son and I really enjoyed our 2 days with Mubeen. His local knowledge is extensive, he was very relaxed and easy to hang out with, speaks very clear English.
We loved the tastes of Mumbai- street food was always cooked fresh at Mubeen's request from vendors and chaibucks.
I highly recommend Mubeen's tours when you are in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Mervyn Tyrer
featured_reviews.review_text:
I , as part of a group of 15 tourists , had the pleasure of meeting Mubeen whilst we were on vacation in Mumbai in November 2018!
His charm , warmth, knowledge and flexibility allowed us all to have the most wonderful first experience of India!!!
I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend his excellent and affordable service to any traveller , who would appreciate his vast understanding and experience!!
Furthermore , having had a financial mishap occur whilst in Mumbai, Mubeen has gone out of his way to liaise and expedite the resolution of the issue !!!
Three cheers for a wonderful guide!!!

featured_reviews.name: Rob Steele
featured_reviews.review_text:
On my very first visit to Mumbai (& in fact India) I was put in contact with Mumbai By Locals by my Hotel and was lucky enough to have Mubeen show up for my City tour to introduce me to the metro area. What a fantastic and personable guide he is-It’s like being taken on a tour with a long lost friend! Mubeen and his driver showed up spot on time and really listened to what I was interested in seeing. He instantly on the fly (over a Masala Chai Tea) at the first stop devised a brilliant itinerary for the next few hours.

Since I was traveling solo, Mubeen graciously offered to take pictures for me during the entire tour. He is an excellent photographer, by the way! We hit the following places: the Queen’s Necklace, Malabar Hill/Hanging Gardens, the Gandhi House & Museum, the Outdoor Laundry, Crawford Market, the old Victoria Station, and finally to the Colaba waterfront & the symbol of Mumbai: the Gateway of India. All along the way he was giving me pointers and recommendations for the rest of my stay in Mumbai and even parts of northern India where I would be traveling next!

I was thoroughly impressed with the quality and experience of my day with Mubeen. The company also offers Street Food tasting tours, Dharavi Slum Tours, Night Market tours and will even guide you to and on Elephanta Island. I had many wonderful guides in India, but Mubeen was my favorite. Enjoy this enchanting city with Mubeen & Mumbai By Locals. Well done!
